summary:
Anambra State stands under Nigeria's national framework. The Same-Sex Marriage (Prohibition) Act applies nationwide and, per Human Rights Watch (October 2016), bans cohabitation between same-sex partners, any public show of a same-sex amorous relationship and the operation of gay organisations, carrying 10 to 14 years' imprisonment; the same reporting documents police torture and arbitrary arrests carried out under the statute.

Anambra lies in Nigeria's southeastern region and is outside the twelve northern states applying Shari'a criminal law, so the death-penalty provisions for sodomy under state Zina provisions do not reach this state. The secular penalty that applies here is up to 14 years' imprisonment, as assessed by the UK Home Office country policy note (June 2025, updated April 2026).

The UK FCDO's current travel advice for Nigeria, relayed by Sahara Reporters (August 2026), warns of attacks, blackmail and intimidation against LGBT+ travellers and up to 14 years' imprisonment for same-sex activity. The same guidance notes death-penalty risk under Shari'a law in northern states, which does not apply in Anambra.

Police use the law against people for how they appear. TimesLIVE (March 2025) reports that a 24-year-old man, Okafor, was stopped by Lagos police, struck in the mouth with a police gun butt and freed only after paying almost half of the 50,000 naira bribe demanded, for 'looking gay'; those affected describe the SSMPA as a weaponised law creating a climate of hostility.

Dating applications carry a specific entrapment risk. Context/Thomson Reuters Foundation (April 2024) documents 'kito' gangs that lure LGBTQ+ Nigerians through Grindr and other apps to meetings where victims are beaten, filmed and blackmailed with threats of outing.

Trans visitors face lethal violence with official misgendering and subsequent impunity. The beaten body of the Abuja trans TikToker 'Abuja Area Mama', a 33-year-old transgender woman, was found on a highway in Abuja in August 2024, hours after she posted about visiting her boyfriend; police said preliminary investigations showed 'a man fully dressed in female clothing', and the Abuja police chief ordered a 'thorough and discreet' investigation. Six months later, in February 2025, The Dial reported that no suspects had been charged.

Cross-dressing has been proposed as a discrete offence. Reuters (September 2022) reports that transgender Nigerians fear proposals to criminalise cross-dressing.

Enforcement takes the form of mass arrests at social venues. Wikipedia's country coverage records that 100-plus party-goers were arrested at a hotel in Asaba, Delta State, in June 2018; 57 young men at Egbeda, Lagos, in August 2018; the 'Warri 67' in Warri, Delta State, in August 2023; and 76 people arrested at a party in Gombe state in October 2023. These are raw counts from a national tally, not per-capita figures, and none of the listed arrests occurred in Anambra.

Care access is chilled by arrest and extortion risk. Many LGBTQ Nigerians fear seeking medical care or reporting crimes, and activists say the Same-Sex Marriage Prohibition Act hampers access to HIV prevention services and forces LGBTQ people and allies to abandon community health and education work.
tangentialFactors:
A 2022 court ruling declared Sections 4(1), 5(2) and 5(3) of the 2013 Act unconstitutional and unenforceable in any part of the country, per Wikipedia's country coverage. The scope and practical effect of that ruling on enforcement in Anambra is not documented in the sources.

Context/Thomson Reuters Foundation (August 2024), marking ten years of the SSMPA, finds the 2014 law has fuelled violence, extortion and discrimination far beyond its scope and has effectively sanctioned abuse, with LGBTQ+ Nigerians reporting lost job prospects and increased attacks since it passed.

LGBTQ-friendly venues face closure. The House of Rainbow Metropolitan Church in Lagos cancelled conferences after members' names and addresses were published in four newspapers on 12 September 2008 and some were threatened, beaten and stoned.

Imprisonment of a prominent transgender woman raised placement questions. Bobrisky (Idris Okuneye) pleaded guilty to four counts of Naira abuse on 5 April 2024 and was sentenced on 12 April 2024 to the maximum six months with no option of fine; she served the term in Kirikiri maximum-security prison, Lagos, and was released on 5 August 2024. Press coverage at sentencing openly asked which prison would hold 'the crossdresser', reflecting discretionary placement. An October 2024 investigative panel dismissed bribery allegations but found that placing her in a maximum-security prison violated the Nigerian Correctional Service Act because she was a first-time offender.
localsOnly:
Anambra is a Nigerian state in the Southeastern region, Igbo-majority, formed in 1976, with capital Awka. Its southern location places it outside the northern zone where the Shari'a criminal-law states sit, so the federal penalties apply in full and the northern Sharia provisions do not reach this state.

LGBTQ+ people in Nigeria have no legal protections and face frequent violence, per Wikipedia's country coverage.

Many LGBTQ Nigerians fear seeking medical care or reporting crimes, and activists say the Same-Sex Marriage Prohibition Act hampers access to HIV prevention services and forces LGBTQ people and allies to abandon community health and education work.
outOfScopeNotes:
No Anambra-specific enforcement incidents, arrests, prosecutions or police conduct are documented in the source inventory. The arrests and venue closures cited are from other Nigerian states and are included only as evidence of the national enforcement pattern.

The scope and practical effect of the 2022 court ruling striking down Sections 4(1), 5(2) and 5(3) of the 2013 Act on ground-level enforcement in Anambra is unresolved in the sources.

Whether the proposed cross-dressing criminalisation reported by Reuters in September 2022 has been enacted is not sourced.

No Anambra-specific data on facility access, document-marker rules or hate-crime protection appears in the inventory.
